title: Man stabbing dog dies after being Tasered by Chilliwack RCMP
subtitle: A man died after being Tasered by police in Chilliwack Wednesday afternoon, say Mounties.
article: A man died after being Tasered by police in Chilliwack Wednesday afternoon, say Mounties.
Members of the Independent Investigations Office of B.C. were called in after the man died and were on scene late that night to determine what happened, said Ed Boettcher, an RCMP spokesman.
Officers with Chilliwack RCMP were sent to a residence on the 9700 block of Oak Street just after 4 p.m., on reports that a man was stabbing a dog, said Boettcher in a news release.
When they arrived, they tried to arrest a male suspect inside the residence.
"It's alleged the suspect struggled with police during their attempts to arrest him," said Boettcher.
It was then that police Tasered the man, then arrested him.
But the man "appeared unresponsive" after being Tasered, said Boettcher, and they began performing CPR on him.
Paramedics soon took over, then transported the man to hospital where he was pronounced dead.
The dog was taken to a veterinarian for treatment, and one officer who was injured on the scene was later treated in hospital, said Boettcher.
Ralph Krenz, a spokesman for the Independent Investigations Office, said a team of five investigators including a forensic specialist had been sent to the scene.
Krenz said they'll be collecting evidence, speaking to witnesses, looking for surveillance video that may exist and interviewing the police officers.
The deceased man's identity has not yet been released.

The man's death comes as Crown prosecutors prepare their case against an officer they allege lied to investigators and perjured himself in relation to the 2007 death of Polish immigrant Robert Dziekanski at Vancouver International Airport. Dziekanski was Tasered by the officer then died.
